corrections.before: Referencing another deployed resource in a Bicep resource declaration creates an implicit dependency; independent resources can deploy in parallel.
corrections.after: Referencing another resource being deployed in the same Bicep deployment creates an implicit dependency; independent resources can deploy in parallel.
corrections.rationale: The dependency guide scopes implicit dependencies to resources in the same deployment, rather than already existing resources.

corrections.before: Setting minimum replicas to one or higher keeps a revision instance running; scale rules determine when replicas increase.
corrections.after: For an active Container Apps revision, minimum replicas of one or higher target keeping an instance running; scale rules determine replica changes. Replica quantities are targets, not availability guarantees.
corrections.rationale: The scale guide explicitly says replica quantities are targets, not guarantees; inactive revisions are not kept running by this setting.

corrections.before: Deployment slots are live apps with separate host names; supported tiers allow content and configuration to be swapped with production.
corrections.after: Deployment slots are live apps with separate host names on Standard, Premium or Isolated plans. Content and swappable configuration can be exchanged between slots, including production; slot-specific settings remain with their slot.
corrections.rationale: The slot guide identifies supported tiers and settings that are not swapped.

corrections.before: Read a Bicep example that references another resource and mark the implicit dependency.
corrections.after: Read a Bicep example that references another resource being deployed in the same deployment and mark the implicit dependency.
corrections.rationale: Avoid implying that references to any existing resource create deployment dependencies.

corrections.before: Use the official what-if procedure in an approved test scope and inspect predicted changes without deploying.
corrections.after: Use a standalone what-if command from the official procedure in an approved test scope and inspect predicted changes without deploying. Review unresolved-expression and template-link limitations; do not use a deployment command with --confirm-with-what-if for this read-only exercise.
corrections.rationale: A standalone what-if previews only; --confirm-with-what-if can proceed into deployment and previews have documented limitations.

corrections.before: Inspect minimum replicas and explain why setting one or higher keeps an instance running.
corrections.after: Inspect an active revision's minimum replicas and explain why setting one or higher targets keeping an instance running. Record that replica quantities are targets, not an availability guarantee.
corrections.rationale: Active revision scope and target limitation are needed for precise scaling behavior.

corrections.before: In an existing nonproduction App Service slot on a supported tier, inspect its separate hostname and validate the staged app. Read the swap procedure and document how a slot swap exchanges content/configuration with production; practice a swap only between approved isolated test slots.
corrections.after: In an existing nonproduction App Service slot on Standard, Premium or Isolated tier, inspect its separate hostname and validate the staged app. Read the swap procedure and identify content, swappable configuration and slot-specific settings; practice a swap only between approved isolated test slots.
corrections.rationale: Do not imply every configuration element swaps, and name supported tiers.

corrections.before: Read the stored access policy procedure for a service SAS; identify how a policy changes its permissions and expiry.
corrections.after: Read the stored access policy procedure for a service SAS; identify how a policy changes permissions and expiry. Stored policies are unsupported for user delegation SAS and account SAS; do not duplicate a policy parameter in the SAS token. A new or changed policy can take up to 30 seconds to become active.
corrections.rationale: These restrictions and propagation caveat are explicit in Define a stored access policy.

corrections.before: For a sample destination, list matching routes and choose the longest prefix before comparing equal-prefix route types.
corrections.after: For a sample destination, inspect effective routes and compare longest-prefix matches and equal-prefix route types. Check the documented preferred system-route exceptions, including virtual-network, peering and service-endpoint routes, before deciding the selected route.
corrections.rationale: The routing guide qualifies normal prefix/type rules with preferred system routes; service endpoint routes cannot be overridden.

corrections.before: A test storage account and container, authorized data access and no sensitive files.
corrections.after: A test storage account and container with no sensitive files. For policy-linked service SAS practice, you need permission to set the container access policy and authorized access to the account key; do not substitute a user delegation SAS or account SAS.
corrections.rationale: A service SAS is signed with Shared Key and the stored policy is set through the resource ACL operation.

corrections.before: Revoke the test policy or SAS, delete test data, and delete a storage account only if you created it solely for this exercise.
corrections.after: Revoke the test policy associated with the service SAS and verify denied access; deleting a SAS token does not revoke it. Delete only disposable test data and an account created solely for this exercise.
corrections.rationale: SAS tokens are client-generated and untracked; policy-linked service SAS can be revoked through the policy.

corrections.before: A local Bicep file; Azure CLI and an authorized test scope only for an optional what-if operation.
corrections.after: A local Bicep file. For optional what-if, use Azure CLI 2.14.0 or later and an authenticated, authorized test scope. Default Provider validation requires deployment-level permissions; CLI 2.76.0 or later offers ProviderNoRbac validation with resource read checks. Consult the current guide for scope and validation permissions.
corrections.rationale: The source defines CLI versions, deployment-equivalent default permissions and newer validation levels.

corrections.before: Remove only disposable container revisions/apps and App Service slots/resources created for this exercise. Preserve any shared plan and other apps that use it. If a permitted isolated slot swap was practiced, verify the intended app version and restore the recorded test configuration.
corrections.after: Deactivate only disposable Container Apps revisions you created, or remove a disposable app when no longer needed. Remove only test App Service slots/resources you created; preserve shared plans and their other apps. After an isolated slot swap, verify the intended app version and restore the recorded test configuration.
corrections.rationale: Revision lifecycle documentation supports activation/deactivation; the exercise should not imply a general manual revision-delete command.

corrections.before: Remove only dedicated disposable VMs, disks and network resources you created. Record existing disks before attachment; never format a disk containing needed data or delete a shared disk. Remove a temporary attachment only after checking the guest mount and data use.
corrections.after: Remove only dedicated disposable VMs, disks and network resources you created. Record existing disks before attachment; never format a disk containing needed data or delete a shared disk. Remove a temporary attachment only after checking the guest mount and data use. Before detaching a Linux data disk, safely unmount it and remove any corresponding /etc/fstab entry; a stale required mount can prevent boot.
corrections.rationale: The disk-attachment guide explicitly cautions that removing a data disk without editing fstab can prevent boot.
